snap: A Monstera with big, split green leaves scattered with creamy white speckles, like stars in a night sky. The pattern is steadier than on most variegated Monsteras. It needs bright, filtered light and a pole to climb. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: The wild Monstera deliciosa grows in the rainforests of southern Mexico and Central America and climbs tree trunks with aerial roots. The Thai Constellation is a cultivated form, named for Thailand, where it is widely said to have been developed. It is multiplied in labs by tissue culture, which keeps its pattern even. With a pole or trellis it can reach 2–3 m indoors.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Give it bright indirect light and let the soil dry out a little between waterings. In dim light the cream speckles fade, and harsh afternoon sun can scorch the pale patches. Water when the top 5 cm of soil is dry, use a chunky, well-draining aroid mix, and keep it above 15°C. Soggy roots rot quickly.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The cream speckles and flecks on dark green leaves look like a scatter of stars, and no two leaves are the same. Because the variegation is spread evenly through the plant, it rarely produces all-white leaves or reverts fully to green, so it grows faster and is easier to keep than a sectored albo. A moss pole makes the leaves larger and more deeply split.
